news.title: Brazil’s study abroad ambitions widen, but information gap holds back demand
news.summary_en: Growing interest in Europe, expanding bilingual schooling and demand for shorter overseas experiences are reshaping Brazil’s outbound student market, according to speakers preparing for The PIE High Brazil.
news.author: Amy Baker

news.title: English UK launches student protection review after provider closures
news.summary_en: English UK has launched a major review of student protection arrangements following a series of large-scale provider closures that have exposed gaps in existing safeguards for international students.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Positively Languages launches with new London and Malta premises
news.summary_en: Positively Languages, formerly Kaplan Languages Group, has formally launched its new brand alongside opening new English language schools in Malta and London.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: Australia loses ground to UK and US in international student race
news.summary_en: Australia is losing ground to the UK and US as a preferred study destination, according to new data from IDP Education.
news.author: Jenna O'Flynn

news.title: UK unis to take £1,010m hit over international student levy
news.summary_en: The UK's upcoming levy on international student fees will batter universities' bottom lines by £110 million more than previously anticipated, according to a new government impact assessment.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: Breaking: UK to extend graduate visa to two years for graduates of “high-compliance universities”
news.summary_en: The UK government will extend the graduate visa to two years for international graduates of “high-compliance universities” with strong labour market outcomes, according to its 2026 Budget.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: IEAA Excellence Awards 2026: Winners announced
news.summary_en: The best of Australia’s international education industry were celebrated at the IEAA Excellence Awards, held during the 40th Australian International Education Conference (AIEC) in Sydney.
news.author: Jenna O'Flynn

news.title: Critics hit back as Canada moves ahead with asylum clampdown
news.summary_en: A policy limiting when refugees in Canada can claim asylum has drawn criticism from the international education sector, with detractors pointing out that there are many legitimate reasons why students may find it unsafe to return to their home country.
news.author: Doug Ronson

news.title: AIEC at 40: Australian international education looks to its next chapter
news.summary_en: International education leaders have gathered in Sydney for the 40th Australian International Education Conference (AIEC), with policy uncertainty, shifting student mobility and AI setting the backdrop for four days of debate about where the sector goes next.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Willkommen! Why international students are choosing Germany
news.summary_en: With The PIE off to Germany this week, Sven Alexander Schottman breaks down why so many international students have decided to call the country home.
news.author: Sven Alexander Schottmann

news.title: Can the UK achieve its international education strategy ambitions under the current BCA framework?
news.summary_en: Following the debate on the recruitment consequences of BCA reform, BUILA chair Stuart Easter considers the changes needed to support effective compliance and the UK’s wider international education ambitions.
news.author: Stuart Easter

news.title: Too big to brake: why Bangladesh and Pakistan escaped the visa brake, and what comes next
news.summary_en: A High Court judgment shows that several key sending countries had a near miss in being included in the UK Home Office's study visa breaks. With fresh compliance requirements looming, universities have been left to manage the largest markets themselves – but could fresh changes be on the horizon? Spencer Withrington investigates.
news.author: Spencer Withrington

news.title: Grads face career readiness “disconnect” as skills take centre stage
news.summary_en: Stakeholders are warning that AI and other technologies are creating a skills "disconnect" in the job market, with today's graduates expected to enter the workforce with the same skill levels as someone who has already gained several years of work experience.
news.author: Beth Kennedy

news.title: Australian universities back new benchmark for education agents
news.summary_en: Six major Australian education providers have joined a new initiative aiming to put student feedback at the heart of how education agents are evaluated and provide stronger evidence of their contribution to international education.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Proposed new OPT fee would decimate the international talent pipeline
news.summary_en: Zuzana Čeplá Wootson, deputy director of federal policy at the Presidents’ Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration, argues that proposed OPT fees would harm students, employers and US competitiveness.
news.author: Zuzana Čeplá Wootson
